text:
maya: Quick perf dump from the canary run — hitting a regression when continuous-batching is enabled and the selector picks the quantized kernel on A100. attaching a short trace + flame snippet. :eyes:

devon: link to flamegraph: https://internal.srv/flame/1745123456 — looks like a lot of time in launch/handshake when kernel switches happen.

sam: numbers?

maya: p50 for chat endpoint at seq=512: baseline (no-contbatch) ~18ms -> canary 35ms. p95 baseline 80ms -> canary 180ms. throughput roughly same, but tail spikes.

kai: that gap screams kernel-path thrash. are we invalidating KV state on every switch?

maya: trace shows KV touch + small memcpy during the switch. selector currently chooses kernel per-batch based on median seq_len and hardware profile. when batches contain mixed seq lengths we flip often. flipping triggers a tiny rebind that touches KV pointers.

anika: idea: hysteresis in the selector (cooldown or require N consecutive decisions before switching). sticky assignment per-worker could help too.

devon: also look at cudaLaunch/cudaStreamSynchronize cost in the warm path — even 0.8–1.2ms per switch adds up if switches are frequent.

sam: any perf of trying sticky?

maya: I ran a quick experiment: sticky kernel per-worker with 30s cooldown. p95 came down from 180ms -> 95ms, p50 ~ unchanged, throughput dropped ~6% under bursty mix. still better tail though. :thumbsup: 

kai: trade-off makes sense. maybe combine with soft-routing: route long sequences to a small dedicated pool so they don't force other workers to switch.

anika: and we should avoid flushing KV cache on compatible kernel variants — maybe we can keep KV layout stable across quantization kernels by using a thin indirection layer.

maya: config I tested: 
```json
{
  "kernel_selector": {
    "mode": "hysteresis",
    "cooldown_seconds": 30,
    "min_votes": 3,
    "sticky_per_worker": true
  },
  "routing": {
    "long_seq_pool_threshold": 384,
    "dedicated_pool_size": 4
  }
}
```

devon: nice. can we make cooldown adaptive? e.g., shorter when load is stable, longer during churn.

maya: yep plan to add simple EWMA on seq_len variance to modulate cooldown. less invasive than full RL.

sam: ops question — is there a config guard to avoid enabling on legacy hw? some GPUs don't like sticky behavior for multi-tenant.

maya: added a guard: hardware.arch in {ampere, hopper} and kernel_variant supports kv-compatible-layout. opsbot triggered a canary deploy with flags on eng-runtime-canary cluster.

opsbot: canary deploy started at 2024-08-16T14:12:30Z (build 2024.8.16-ker-hyst). monitoring hooks active.

devon: next steps: 1) add adaptive cooldown EWMA, 2) work on reducing cudaLaunch handshakes (kernel warmstart refactor), 3) evaluate indirection for KV layout to avoid copies.

anika: I'll prototype routing to a small long-seq pool and measure 95/99 tails.

sam: add a test harness that simulates mixed-seqlen arrival patterns so we can try variations offline.

maya: will push the EWMA PR and benchmark. thanks all.

devon: fyi I'll capture a perf regression ticket and tag runtime/autotune/kernel for tracking. :memo:
